new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand, database-wide: in Nivens's comparative Aru data (which include Lorang), the default is stress on the penultimate syllable, with final stress when the final syllable contains a mid vowel; any form that departs from this is written with an acute accent. Lorang forms so flagged in the book are maŋár 'sky', saŋír 'rotten', gúʤen 'rain', (wúney) 'mango', ɸúʤa 'fruit' and (m-ɸúlar) 'see'; the many unmarked Lorang forms (kawa, dubu, yabay, ɸulan, ɸatu, yemal, ʔita..) are penultimate by the convention. Note that maŋár and saŋír are final-stressed without a mid vowel, and gúʤen/ɸúʤa are penultimate-stressed despite a mid-vowel final, so the convention is not fully predictive for Lorang; no Lorang-specific description exists.
new_statements.exceptions: Only implicitly, via the acute on 'unexpected stress': for Lorang maŋár 'sky', saŋír 'rotten', gúʤen 'rain', (wúney) 'mango', ɸúʤa 'fruit', (m-ɸúlar) 'see'.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated lexical items (comparative wordlist forms, citation forms) in a historical-comparative volume; no statement about phrase-level or morphologically complex words.
new_statements.identity_note: Lorang (lora1237, ISO lrn), one village (Lorang) on Koba Island in the Barakai Strait, central Aru; not to be confused with Lola (lola1248, Leer/Penambula/Barakan islands), which shares the atlas page with it and is what Erniati et al. 2022 mistakenly call 'Desa Lola' when locating Lorang. Badan Bahasa (2017, as reported by Erniati et al.) classes Lorang as a dialect of 'bahasa Barakai' alongside Gomo Gomo, Mariri and Koba, contrary to Hughes 1987 and Glottolog, which treat it as a separate language closest to the Koba dialect of Dobel (dobe1235). The Grimes & Edwards 2026 statement is a convention for the whole Nivens Proto-Aru database, not a description of Lorang specifically.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item and it is the one checked. Spot-check of the whole scanned text for stress terms found nothing about Lorang or any Aru language; the only prosodic remarks are Luhu p. 96 and Kaibobo p. 98 (both already reported by the reader, both Seram), plus passing mentions the reader did not list that are not stress statements: Saparua Malay differs from Ambon Malay 'largely in intonation patterns' (p. 92), Kairatu Alune changed *a to e 'in antepenultimate syllables' (p. 99), a NW-Seram language deletes/devoices high vowels 'of trisyllabic words in the penultimate position' (p. 101). None is a placement rule and none concerns lora1237.

Sec. 2.2.3.6 'Lorang' (pp. 98-99): just over 200 speakers, village of Lorang on Koba Island, smallest language community in the Aru-Kei-Tanimbar area, no dialect variation; sec. 2.2.3: Lorang relates at 80% to the Koba dialect of Dobel and 79% to Benjina (Wokam/Manombai), designated a separate language.
